question: In a pedigree of an autosomal dominant trait it is observed that:

options.opa: The trait appears more frequently in males.
options.opb: The unaffected people do not transmit the trait.
options.opc: The trait tends to skip generations.
options.opd: The affected people have both affected parents.
options.ope: The trait tends to appear in the progeny of related parents.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait appears in both males and females equally" -> "trait does not appear more frequently in males" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "unaffected individuals do not carry the trait" -> "unaffected people do not transmit the trait" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait appears in every generation" -> "trait does not skip generations" -> 10%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "one affected parent can transmit the trait" -> "affected people may have one or both affected parents" -> 30%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait appears regardless of parental relation" -> "trait does not specifically appear in progeny of related parents" -> 15%
analysis: In a pedigree of an autosomal dominant trait, the key characteristic is that the trait does not skip generations. Unaffected individuals do not carry the trait and therefore do not transmit it to their offspring. This is because autosomal dominant traits require only one copy of the dominant allele to express the trait, and if an individual does not express the trait, they do not have the dominant allele to pass on.
